findings.body: ZADD (and later ZSCAN) against the existing Set raises a WRONGTYPE Redis error, causing affected ingestion batches or flushes to fail and leaving already-buffered spans unflushable until the old keys expire.
findings.failure_mode: Buffered span processing fails at Redis command execution for pre-upgrade segment keys.
findings.impact: ZADD (and later ZSCAN) against the existing Set raises a WRONGTYPE Redis error, causing affected ingestion batches or flushes to fail and leaving already-buffered spans unflushable until the old keys expire.
findings.root_cause: The patch changes the persistent Redis collection type from Set to Sorted Set in place without migrating keys that already exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a versioned Redis key namespace or add a deployment migration/compatibility path that reads and drains Set-backed keys before writing or scanning ZSet-backed keys.
findings.title: Migrate existing span-buffer keys before changing their Redis type
findings.trigger: A worker running this version encounters a span-buffer segment key created by the previous version, which is a Redis Set and can remain for up to its configured TTL during or after a rolling deployment.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch changes `sadd` to `zadd` at line 197 and `zscan` is used in `_load_segment_data`. Existing keys created by prior version are Redis Sets. Running ZADD/ZSCAN against a Set key raises WRONGTYPE error. Rolling deployment scenario is realistic trigger with concrete Redis error impact.

findings.body: The configured limit is no longer enforced: up to 1000 spans are retained and flushed instead of the prior oversized-segment handling, so deployments that set a smaller limit can exceed their intended memory and downstream payload bounds.
findings.failure_mode: A caller-specified resource bound is silently ignored.
findings.impact: The configured limit is no longer enforced: up to 1000 spans are retained and flushed instead of the prior oversized-segment handling, so deployments that set a smaller limit can exceed their intended memory and downstream payload bounds.
findings.root_cause: The new eviction threshold is hard-coded to 1000 while the existing max_segment_spans setting is no longer checked during loading.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass self.max_segment_spans to the Lua script and use that argument as the eviction threshold (or retain the Python-side configured-limit check).
findings.title: Honor the configured maximum segment span count
findings.trigger: A SpansBuffer is constructed with max_segment_spans below 1000, for example 10, and a segment receives more spans than that configured limit.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 62 shows hardcoded `if span_count > 1000 then` eviction threshold. SpansBuffer constructor accepts `max_segment_spans` parameter (default 1001) but this value is never passed to the Lua script. Configured limits below 1000 are silently ignored, allowing more spans than intended.

findings.body: math.floor/math.ceil receives a datetime object and raises TypeError while constructing cursor metadata, returning a server error instead of an audit-log page.

findings.impact: math.floor/math.ceil receives a datetime object and raises TypeError while constructing cursor metadata, returning a server error instead of an audit-log page.
findings.root_cause: OptimizedCursorPaginator applies numeric rounding directly to the model field value instead of converting datetime keys to numeric timestamps.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement DateTimePaginator-compatible key extraction, converting datetime values to timestamps before floor/ceil, or subclass DateTimePaginator for this endpoint.
findings.title: Convert AuditLogEntry datetimes before applying numeric cursor rounding
